results.title: Saving Privacy from History
results.snippet: We have been panicking about privacy for over a hundred years now, since at least 1890, when Warren and Brandeis wrote their famous article, “The Right to Privacy,” the foundational text of the tort law of privacy.

results.title: Privacy Before 'the Right to Privacy': Truthful Libel and the Earliest Underpinnings of Privacy in the United States
results.snippet:
The Right to Privacy, written in 1890, is perhaps the most famous law review article ever published in the United States.
In twenty-seven pages, Samuel Warren and William Brandeis argued that the time was ripe for new legal protection in the form of a privacy tort, one that would protect people from the prying ways of increasingly intrusive, technologically savvy journalists.
